# Phase Two — Gevurah: Critique and Failure Guards

The Awtsmoos gives limitless light, while Awtsmoos.com demands a vessel that never calls a silent hang success.

1. Never merely increase queue sizes; that delays the same failure and increases memory risk.
2. Never add arbitrary sleeps as the backpressure mechanism.
3. Never swallow worker errors while awaiting frame acknowledgement.
4. Every frame request must eventually resolve, reject, or time out with stage/index evidence.
5. Avoid modifying canonical renderer semantics while fixing encoder flow.
6. Do not replace the proven MP4 worker with ffmpeg until the actual defect is understood.
7. If a shared video helper is touched, rewrite the whole file and split dense responsibilities rather than partial patching.
8. Keep browser worker source below 120 lines by extracting queue/drain helpers.
9. Release/close ImageBitmap and VideoFrame resources deterministically.
10. Report queue depth, frame index, timestamp, and stage at least at coarse intervals.
11. Long render test must exceed the encoder queue threshold; 3 seconds at 12fps is already enough but a 30-second fixture is stronger.
12. Full proof must use the canonical 180-second movie, not a synthetic pattern.
13. Full output must be independently probed by ffprobe.
14. Frame witnesses must be derived from the actual MP4, not directly from the canonical renderer.
15. Mobile UI proof must include actual interaction and console inspection.
16. Existing green Node tests remain required after every source repair.
17. Do not rewrite unrelated peer files in the dirty shared workspace.
18. Fresh-hash every existing file immediately before full rewrite.
19. Refactor over-120 neighbors only after their importers are traced.
20. Completion requires stale plan/evidence artifacts to be reconciled with reality.
